purpose: Final shortlist from the 2026-08 market-wide RAG storage screen, selected after a strict correction pass. Classification terminology is deliberate and must be preserved exactly in any downstream reference: these are SCREENING-level results only, not production or benchmark verdicts. No adapter code has been written for either finalist; no benchmark, lifecycle test, or concurrency mechanism has been implemented or executed.

classification_legend.SCREENING_PASS: Every named hard gate resolves favorably at the market-comparison/documentation-research level.
classification_legend.BENCHMARK_PENDING: The BENCHMARK_GATE requirements (Recall@10, latency, real retrieval-quality metrics, lifecycle matrix, concurrency torture test - see requirements.json) have not been executed for this candidate.
classification_legend.PRODUCTION_NOT_APPROVED: Explicit, standing statement that screening-level evidence does not constitute a production readiness verdict. No implementer may self-certify production readiness from this document alone.
classification_legend.SCREENING_PASS_WITH_CAPACITY_RISK: Every named hard gate except capacity/growth-headroom resolves favorably; that one gate remains genuinely open pending measurement.

finalists.what_could_overturn_this: Pinecone's concurrency protocol or consistency mechanism not holding up once actually implemented and tested; failing the dense-ANN recall (>=0.98) or real retrieval-quality benchmarks; an undiscovered capacity/quota interaction once real ingestion volume is measured.

finalists.architecture: Neon pgvector dense vectors (split variant) + existing Convex lexical/canonical layer
finalists.variant_note: The SPLIT variant specifically (Neon holds dense vectors only; Convex retains the existing lexical/canonical layer) - NOT the all-in-one 'Neon PostgreSQL + pgvector + PostgreSQL FTS' variant, which was also considered but has meaningfully worse storage headroom for the same 500MB cap since it would also carry a full-text index.
why_selected: Rests on the most battle-tested underlying technology of any candidate studied: pgvector has been a real, widely-deployed Postgres extension since 2021, a meaningfully lower novel-implementation-risk profile than Turso's newer DiskANN (the exact risk class that sank the prior candidate).

Idle-durability gate is resolved with real, current, official, specific evidence: automatic 5-minute scale-to-zero, sub-second resume, fully automatic with no manual action ever - years-long product positioning, not a recently-changed policy.
Real ACID transactions give it the strongest native (not application-level-workaround) answer to the concurrency invariant of any candidate studied.
Fails closed on overage (writes blocked / compute suspended until upgrade, no card on file).

Native tsvector/GIN full-text search is core, GA PostgreSQL - a credible fallback location for lexical retrieval if the split architecture doesn't hold up, though the shortlisted design keeps lexical in Convex.

finalists.what_could_overturn_this: Growth headroom turning out too tight in practice once measured; failing the dense-ANN recall or real retrieval-quality benchmarks; the pgvector HNSW index build behaving differently than expected at the real 20,652-row scale (the same class of risk that sank Turso, though pgvector's maturity makes this less likely).

convergent_finding: Both finalists independently converge on the same high-level architectural shape: an external store holding dense vectors ONLY, with Convex retaining the existing lexical/canonical layer - not an all-in-one vendor. This is a real finding, not a coincidence forced by the write-up: every all-in-one candidate researched (Weaviate dense+BM25, TiDB, the Neon-with-Postgres-FTS variant) carries either an unresolved hard gate or a vendor-flagged maturity concern that the split shape avoids by depending on less from any single new vendor.
